title: I Built a Blog and Forgot to Write
excerpt: Hello there! It’s been a while since I last wrote something 🙃.
content_html:
Hello there! It’s been a while since I last wrote something 🙃.

Part of it was just life getting busy, but I think a bigger factor was how hard I made it for myself to write anything. You see, as a proper engineer I had the most efficient personal blog. The content was written in markdown, made into a static site using 11ty, filled with custom scripts to process images and videos, custom CSS for fonts, nice clean templates and hand-crafted theme, and scripts to deploy everything with a single npm command.

Well, it was perfect, minimalist, fast, very aesthetically pleasing for me (that is, the codebase). Except that I didn't write anything. It was too hard. I had to make a new folder inside _content/ and then a .md file named the same as the parent folder (have you seen how ugly 5 index.md tabs look? not knowing what is what?).

And then inside the markdown I had to add a front matter with a slug with the same name as the parent folder and filename. You can already see how stuck I felt doing even something as simple as changing the title of a post.

But then came handling images or videos: how big are they? what is the correct ![image.png] to write? did I place images in the global /images folder or are they siblings with the post?

Ugh!

By the time I was done with all of that I had already forgotten what I wanted to write about.

So then the issue was obviously 11ty. If only I had more control over how things work so that I could fine-tune everything exactly the way I wanted it... YES! I'll build my own static site generator. How hard could it be!? (famous last words...)

So I did, or rather, so I started and never finished...

I thought that a clean UNIX-philosophy static site generator would do: pandoc can convert markdown files to HTML, some bash scripts to iterate through my markdown files, inject some CSS and Bob's your uncle. But wait. How do I make an index page listing all the article titles and dates and sort them? well I need to read the front matter for all the posts. But wait, how do I generate an RSS/Atom feed? maybe a template? I need the data from the front matter of the posts for this and a templating engine. How do I filter to exclude drafts? how do I serve? can I have hot reload?

Yeah, how hard can it be!

But then I realized something: I was mixing up the process of building an efficient, performant, featureful blogging engine with the goal of writing posts! 🤦‍♂️

🛠️ Process vs Results

This might be obvious to some of you but it wasn't for me until recently: in life there are things I care about the process and others that I care about the results, and mixing the two has caused me so much pain.

Two examples, 3D printing and Linux.

I got into 3D printing a few years ago. It was so fun to be able to imagine physical objects, see them on a screen and then have them as actual objects in the world. I printed so many useful things to organize my office, showcase my mechanical keyboards, hold the keys and paper towel, all kinds of cool things. But then, as a proper tinkerer, I wanted more control over my 3D printer. So I swapped out the main board, flashed a custom firmware, connected a Raspberry Pi to it, added a webcam, tweaked the motors and added some extra sensors... but completely lost my interest in 3D printing...

You see, 3D printing became so hard: what was that local DNS I assigned to the 3D printer RPI? what nozzle does it have at the moment? is the RPI even on? the local website of the custom firmware is not responding, the filament is not sticking, did I run that bed leveling thing and copy/pasted the values into the calibration thing?

The whole thing went from putting an SD card in the 3D printer and printing, to a whole bunch of steps because of all the control I had. Sure, my 3D printer was arguably more powerful, but at the cost of so much more complexity. And I've now realized that regarding 3D printing, I couldn't care less about the process. I just want the prints.

With Linux the story was a bit similar. I've used Arch since forever. It is an awesome distro where all the newest OSS software lands first. You can customize it to your heart's content, to the point of knowing exactly how many processes are running after boot, having a full working system with like 400MB of RAM usage, and having your own rice with everything just perfect, precisely pixel perfect.

That was fun and all until I had to do something productive with my computer! Then the custom stuff just became friction. X needed some service running to share screen, and Y didn't work with a tiling window manager. I also needed to add a script to launch Z because my custom launcher didn't recognize the .desktop files the program came with...

I installed Fedora and everything just worked. It was awesome. Again I had confused wanting the process vs wanting the results.

I think there's more nuance to it, but as a tinkerer/maker/engineer/hacker/what have you, I'm used to enjoying the process: building the thing, knowing how things work under the hood, being in full control and the power understanding it entails, realizing a vision, overcoming difficulties, learning new things and bending the computer/device/situation to my will.

All of that is great, but when embarking on something new, knowing if I'm embarking on it for the process/journey or for the results has been saving me some headaches lately. As an example, I'm currently picking up Linear Algebra. The journey is arduous but I'm doing this for the results. I need this to better understand Statistical Learning. On the other hand, I'm also learning Real Analysis. It could be useful someday, but I'm doing it because I love the journey. Analysis is beautiful and elegant, infinite series are weird and mysterious (Fourier series are straight up wizardry!), Euler was an absolute genius, the landscapes are gorgeous, and I'm in it for the journey!

🤝 Concessions

So then, here I am actually writing! This blog is still by any measure nerdy and opinionated, it is still a static site built with Zola, still deploying to Bunny by GitHub Actions... but now I don't care that much about the aesthetics of the codebase. I'm using Sveltia CMS to manage content. So I went from creating a file, wrangling front matter, index.md tab archeology (the index.md files are still there... I just don't see them) to a textbox on a website. Write some text, see a preview, drag and drop images, and publish. It went from a "project" to a "textbox". Sure, it seems like something small, all of this just to say that I'm now using a CMS? but the fact is I'm actually writing again 😃!

This year I decided to participate in The Complete Roguelike Tutorial 2026 on Reddit, because I've never completed a game... and I want to know how that works. (read, process :-D ) I'll likely be posting about that soon!

blocks.html_en: All of that is great, but when embarking on something new, knowing if I'm embarking on it for the process/journey or for the results has been saving me some headaches lately. content_html_zh:
你好呀！ 自从我上次写东西以来已经有一段时间了。

部分原因是生活变得忙碌，但我认为更重要的因素是我让自己很难写任何东西。 你看，作为一名合格的工程师，我拥有最高效的个人博客。 内容是用 Markdown 编写的，使用 11ty 制作成静态站点，其中包含处理图像和视频的自定义脚本、字体的自定义 CSS、漂亮干净的模板和手工制作的主题，以及使用单个 npm 命令部署所有内容的脚本。

嗯，它是完美的、简约的、快速的、对我来说非常美观（即代码库）。 只不过我什么也没写。 太难了。 我必须在 _content/ 中创建一个新文件夹，然后创建一个与父文件夹同名的 .md 文件（你见过 5 个 index.md 选项卡看起来有多难看吗？ 不知道什么是什么？）。

然后在 Markdown 中，我必须添加一个前面的内容，其中包含一个与父文件夹和文件名同名的 slug。 您已经可以看到我在做一些简单的事情（例如更改帖子标题）时感到多么困难。

但接下来是处理图像或视频：它们有多大？ ![image.png] 正确的写法是什么？ 我是否将图像放置在全局 /images 文件夹中，还是它们与帖子是同级的？

Ugh!

当我完成所有这些时，我已经忘记了我想写什么。

那么问题显然是11ty。 如果我能更好地控制事情的运作方式，这样我就可以按照我想要的方式微调一切...... 是的！ 我将构建自己的静态站点生成器。 这能有多难！ （著名的遗言......）

所以我做到了，或者更确切地说，所以我开始了，但从未完成......

我认为一个干净的 UNIX 哲学静态站点生成器就可以了：pandoc 可以将 markdown 文件转换为 HTML，一些 bash 脚本可以迭代我的 markdown 文件，注入一些 CSS，Bob 是你的叔叔。 但等等。 如何制作一个索引页，列出所有文章标题和日期并对它们进行排序？ 好吧，我需要阅读所有帖子的前言。 但是等等，如何生成 RSS/Atom 提要？ 也许是一个模板？ 我需要帖子前面的数据和模板引擎。 如何过滤以排除草稿？ 我该如何服务？ 我可以热重载吗？

是啊，哪有那么难啊！

但后来我意识到一件事：我混淆了构建高效、高性能、功能丰富的博客引擎的过程与撰写帖子的目标！ 🤦‍♂️

🛠️过程与结果

这对你们中的一些人来说可能是显而易见的，但直到最近才对我来说：在生活中，有些事情我关心过程，有些事情我关心结果，而将两者混合在一起给我带来了很大的痛苦。

两个例子，3D 打印和 Linux。

几年前我开始接触 3D 打印。 能够想象物理对象，在屏幕上看到它们，然后将它们作为世界上的实际对象，真是太有趣了。 我打印了很多有用的东西来整理我的办公室，展示我的机械键盘，握住按键和纸巾，各种很酷的东西。 但后来，作为一名真正的修补匠，我想要更好地控制我的 3D 打印机。 所以我更换了主板，刷新了自定义固件，将 Raspberry Pi 连接到它，添加了网络摄像头，调整了电机并添加了一些额外的传感器...... 但我对3D打印完全失去了兴趣......

你看，3D 打印变得如此困难：我分配给 3D 打印机 RPI 的本地 DNS 是什么？ 目前它有什么喷嘴？ RPI 还在吗？ 自定义固件的本地网站没有响应，灯丝没有粘住，我是否运行了床调平程序并将这些值复制/粘贴到校准程序中？

由于我拥有所有控制权，整个过程从将 SD 卡放入 3D 打印机并进行打印，到了一大堆步骤。 当然，我的 3D 打印机可以说更强大，但代价是更加复杂。 现在我意识到，对于 3D 打印，我不能不关心过程。 我只想要印刷品。

Linux 的情况有点类似。 我从始至终都在使用Arch。 这是一个很棒的发行版，所有最新的 OSS 软件都首先登陆。 您可以根据自己的喜好进行定制，准确了解启动后有多少进程正在运行，拥有一个大约 400MB RAM 使用量的完整工作系统，并拥有自己的米饭，一切都很完美，精确的像素完美。

这很有趣，直到我不得不用我的电脑做一些富有成效的事情！ 然后定制的东西就变成了摩擦。 X 需要运行一些服务来共享屏幕，而 Y 无法使用平铺窗口管理器。 我还需要添加一个脚本来启动 Z，因为我的自定义启动器无法识别程序附带的 .desktop 文件...

我安装了 Fedora，一切正常。 太棒了。 我再次混淆了想要过程和想要结果。

我认为其中还有更多细微差别，但作为一名修补匠/制造商/工程师/黑客/你有什么，我习惯于享受这个过程：构建东西，了解事物在幕后如何工作，完全控制和理解它所需要的力量，实现愿景，克服困难，学习新事物并将计算机/设备/情况屈服于我的意愿。

所有这些都很棒，但是当开始做一些新的事情时，知道我是为了过程/旅程还是为了结果而开始它最近让我省去了一些头痛。 举个例子，我目前正在学习线性代数。 虽然过程很艰辛，但我这样做是为了结果。 我需要这个来更好地理解统计学习。 另一方面，我也在学习实分析。 有一天它可能会有用，但我这样做是因为我喜欢这个旅程。 分析美丽而优雅，无穷级数怪异而神秘（傅里叶级数简直就是魔法！），欧拉绝对是天才，风景美丽，我正在其中踏上旅程！

🤝 优惠

那么，我真的在这里写了！ 从任何角度来看，这个博客仍然是书呆子和固执己见，它仍然是一个用 Zola 构建的静态站点，仍然通过 GitHub Actions 部署到 Bunny... 但现在我不太关心代码库的美观。 我正在使用 Sveltia CMS 来管理内容。 所以我从创建文件、争论前题、index.md 选项卡考古（index.md 文件仍然存在...... 我只是没有看到它们）到网站上的文本框。 编写一些文本，查看预览，拖放图像，然后发布。 它从“项目”变成了“文本框”。 当然，这似乎是一件小事，所有这一切只是为了说明我现在正在使用 CMS？ 但事实是我又在写了😃！

今年我决定参加 Reddit 上的 The Complete Roguelike Tutorial 2026，因为我从未完成过游戏...... 我想知道这是如何运作的。 （阅读，处理：-D）我可能很快就会发布相关内容！
